full_caption: Quarrytown Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellant, v. Kingsmere Realty Trust, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Quarrytown Capital Servicing, LLC appeals the denial by the Stillwater County Board of Adjustment of a use variance permitting operation of a veterinary clinic at 1833 Mill Race Way, Stillwater, CW, a parcel zoned R-1 single-family residential.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The board's findings must be sufficient to permit meaningful review. Conclusory recitals tracking the language of the ordinance, without reference to record evidence, require remand.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Discontinuance for 9 months is presumed abandonment under Section 19.7 of the ordinance. The presumption is rebutted by proof of an intent to resume coupled with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The parcel is 580 square feet, irregular in shape, and burdened by a drainage easement across 10 percent of its buildable area. Those are conditions of the land and not of the owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Hardship must arise from the land itself and not from the owner's personal circumstances or from a self-created condition. Purchase with knowledge of the restriction is a factor but is not, standing alone, disqualifying.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A use variance requires proof of unnecessary hardship: that the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any permitted use, that the hardship is unique to the parcel, and that the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a prerequisite to judicial review. A facial constitutional challenge to the ordinance is excepted from that requirement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Vested rights against a subsequent ordinance arise where the developer, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has made substantial expenditures. Quarrytown Capital Servicing, LLC expended $455,000 on site work before the moratorium was adopted.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The denial is vacated and the matter remanded to the Board for findings addressing the drainage easement and the shape of the parcel.

sections.heading: RIDER A — VARIANCE APPLICATION AND FINDINGS REQUIRED
sections.text: An application for a use variance shall be granted only upon written findings, supported by substantial evidence in the record, that: (1) the property cannot yield a reasonable return in any use permitted in the district; (2) the hardship arises from conditions unique to the parcel and not generally applicable in the district; (3) the hardship was not self-created; and (4) the variance will not alter the essential character of the locality. Findings that merely recite the language of this Rider without reference to record evidence are insufficient.

sections.heading: RIDER B — CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL
sections.text: Any approval is subject to the following conditions, each of which runs with the land: hours of operation limited to 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.; off-street parking of not fewer than 48 spaces; a landscaped buffer of not less than 25 feet along every boundary abutting a residential district; exterior lighting shielded and directed downward; and no exterior signage exceeding 12 square feet. Violation of any condition voids the approval after notice and an opportunity to cure.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $500,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.
